label: Financial Records
description: Minimal starter vocabulary for a financial-records tenant. Deliberately small and generic: it exists to prove the platform is aimed by configuration, not to guess at a client's retention schedule.
_editing: This file is DATA. Edit it with a text editor — no code changes needed.
document_types = what a document IS. requirements = the checklist line items it CLOSES.
claim_types + claim_rules = what a document ASSERTS and which requirement that opens.
closes                  = the requirement slugs a document of this TYPE normally closes. An EMPTY list is a real
answer, not an omission: an invoice or a receipt is filed and searched, and closes no
owner                   = the department that owns this type's renewals. Must be one of owner_labels below.
extraction_instructions = the document-type layer of the extraction prompt. A string, or an array of lines.
owner_labels        = the departments this vertical has. LABELS ONLY — a human adds the actual people.
requirement_packets = named sets of requirements, applied to ONE counterparty at a time. Nothing is seeded from these.
teach               = the worked example the setup wizard teaches one concept with.
modules             = which parts of the portal a tenant seeded from this pack starts with.
Seeding is additive (INSERT OR IGNORE) — re-running never overwrites edits made in the admin UI.
_deliberately_omitted: Retention PERIODS (7 years, permanent, ...). We do not know this client's schedule and a wrong number in a compliance tool is worse than no number. Retention is a per-document field, not a vocabulary row, and is parked in backlog.md.
Jurisdiction- or framework-specific checklists (SOX, GAAP/IFRS, IRS publication cites). Those are a real deliverable, not a starter guess.
Expiry / renewal defaults per document type — document_types has no renewal columns today (renewal lives per document), so any default here would be fiction.
A large claim taxonomy. Only the two claims that unambiguously open a named document are seeded.

spec_tests / spec_limits — and this omission is the format working, not a gap. A spec limit judges a numeric ANALYTE RESULT printed on a certificate against an acceptance threshold. A bank statement has no analyte. Seeding an empty synonym map here would have been the same mistake as seeding six requirements onto every supplier: configuration that looks present and judges nothing.
supplier_requirements — a new tenant has zero counterparties, so there is nothing to apply a packet to. Packets are defined below and applied one counterparty at a time.
owner_routes — a route needs a real recipient. This pack supplies department LABELS; a human supplies the people.
extraction_context — tenants.extraction_context (0072) is a whole-block replacement, so a pack writing it would overwrite an edited block on every re-run.

document_types.name: Invoice
extraction_instructions: An invoice is a demand for payment against one counterparty and one period. Everything on it belongs to that single transaction.

- supplier_name is the company ISSUING the invoice — the letterhead and the remit-to block will agree. customer_name is the BILL TO / SOLD TO party. Getting these the wrong way round files the document against the wrong counterparty.

- Capture the invoice number, the invoice date and the due date under the labels the document prints for them. A payment-terms string ("Net 30", "2/10 Net 30") is captured as printed and never converted into a due date the invoice did not state.
- Emit the line items as a table named "line_items" using the document's own column headings (commonly Description, Quantity, Unit Price, Amount).

- Copy every amount EXACTLY as printed, including its currency symbol or code where one appears. Never convert a currency, never re-scale a figure, and never compute a total the invoice did not print.
- A purchase-order number, contract number or job number printed on the invoice is a REFERENCE to another document. Capture it under its own label; it does not make this document a purchase order.
- document_expires_on is null. An invoice does not expire; it is paid, disputed or written off.

document_types.name: Bank Statement
document_types.description: Periodic statement from a financial institution.
extraction_instructions: A bank statement covers one ACCOUNT for one PERIOD, and both of those are the point of filing it.
- Capture the institution name, the account name and the statement period start and end dates as printed.
- The account number is nearly always MASKED on the statement ("****4471"). Capture it exactly as shown, mask included. Never reconstruct, unmask or pad an account number.

- Capture the opening and closing balances under the labels the statement prints. Do not compute either one from the transaction list, and do not correct a balance that does not appear to foot — a statement that does not reconcile is a finding, not a transcription error to fix.

- Emit the transactions as a table named "transactions" with the statement's own columns (commonly Date, Description, Debit, Credit, Balance). Keep debits and credits in the columns they were printed in; never net them into a single signed figure.
- Interest, fees and adjustments are ordinary transaction rows unless the statement gives them their own summary block, in which case capture that block under its printed heading.
- document_expires_on is null: a statement covers a period that has already closed.

document_types.name: Contract
extraction_instructions: An executed agreement. The parties, the term and the signatures are what makes it filable; the body is prose and is not a field.

- Capture every named party with the role the contract gives it ("Supplier", "Vendor", "Client", "Licensor"). supplier_name is the counterparty; customer_name is us. Where the preamble defines short names ("...hereinafter 'the Supplier'"), capture the legal entity name, not the short name.

- Capture the effective date, the term and the expiry or renewal date under the labels the contract prints. document_expires_on is the end of the CURRENT term only. An auto-renewal clause is captured as text under its own label and never turned into a future date the document did not state.
- Capture the notice period for termination as printed, in the units printed.

- Capture each signature block: signatory name, title, and the date beside that signature. An unsigned or undated signature block is captured as empty — it is the single most important thing to report honestly about an agreement, and inferring a date from elsewhere in the document destroys it.
- Amounts, rates and minimums stay exactly as printed, with the currency the contract printed. Never annualize, prorate or convert.
- Exhibits and schedules are part of the same document. Where a schedule is a table, emit it under its own printed name.

requirement_packets.name: Counterparty Onboarding
requirement_packets.description: What a new vendor or contractor owes before they are paid. Applied one counterparty at a time — the same discipline as the food-safety pack, for the same reason: applied in bulk it becomes a checklist that is uniform and wrong.

teach.decoy_reason: A reconciliation QUOTES the ledger balance it is reconciling to. It is not the ledger, and filing it against the General Ledger line item leaves that line item looking closed by a document that contains none of the detail. A document TYPE is not a checklist REQUIREMENT — that is the one idea this screen exists to teach.
teach._note: A bank reconciliation closes exactly ONE line item, and the sample is scaled to that rather than padded to match the FSQA pack's nine. What it does carry is the decoy's bait, printed in full: the general ledger balance for account 1010-00, quoted by account number, next to a note saying the ledger detail is not reproduced. The temptation and its answer are both on the page.
